engagement_title: Continental Cup 2026 full squad card run: eighteen squad portraits brought to one pitch-side look, the printer's team set card rebuilt into a live merge, and the run delivered as an ordered press file, per player files and an editable squad chart
vertical: Sports, fitness and recreation, licensed tournament collectible trading cards distributed through a national licensing partner into grocery, newsstand and hobby (Continental Cup 2026, a touring North American and European club tournament)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com poster commission quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, a high impact football tournament star poster asked for with cinematic, high contrast floodlit lighting and both print and web delivery. Every real element is laundered: the competition is the coined fictional Continental Cup 2026, the athletes are clearly fictional (Diego Solano, Marco Ferraz, Theo Rocher, Luka Petrov, Andre Mensah, Rafael Duarte, Nikolai Ivanic, Samuel Okoye and the rest of the coined squad), and no real club, nation, flag, emblem, competition, sponsor, camera, editing product or social platform is named anywhere. The ledger's own repositioning note concedes that the poster as posted sat on a single surface and was not the fuller commission. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest job is: a printer's flat press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live InDesign merge template headlessly, one record per page is confirmed behaviour, per record named single card files are producible by two verified routes, and an authored HTML page becomes a native editable Express document. So this is the commission that client genuinely needed once the licensing partner bought the whole squad rather than one hero: a variable data print run off photography that has to be brought to one look first, with the identity recovered rather than reinvented, and the trade stand chart handed back editable.
client_one_liner: The licensing partner has taken the whole squad, so we owe them eighteen cards instead of eight, and all we have is one PDF from last season's printer and a roster export nobody has ever read.
client_brief:
Continental Cup 2026, full squad card run

Our licensing partner has taken the whole squad. Last season we printed eight featured players. This season every player in the squad gets a card and the whole set ships as one run.

The pictures. Most of the squad was shot pitch side across three evenings at the ground. Four players missed that shoot and were photographed later in a corridor under the house lighting. They do not look like one set and they have to. These cards sit next to each other in a sleeve inside the pack, so a player who looks like he was photographed somewhere else is the first thing a collector sees. We want each player cleanly off the ground behind him, on the dark card field, and the partner also wants versions with nothing behind them for their own coloured tiles.

The card. We do not have the design file. What we have is the PDF the printer ran last season, the team set card at its proper trim. The layout is right and we want to keep it. Each card carries the player name, squad number, position, club line and set year, plus the photograph and our tournament mark.

The mark. It only exists on printed things now. There is a photograph of a sponsor board in the folder with the mark on it. We need it back as artwork we can use at any size, on the cards and everywhere else.

The roster comes out of the licensing database as a spreadsheet. It is the contractual copy, so what it says goes on the card as written. Nobody has read it.

What we need back. One press file for the printer with the whole squad in it, in squad order. One file per player for the partner, named to the player, because they distribute them individually. Proofs at real print quality that our licensing people can sign off. And the squad chart for the trade stand, as something we can edit ourselves next season.

A note on what you did and anything we should know about using the mark.
price_band_and_audience: A licensed flagship tournament pack retailing around fourteen dollars, collector aged sixteen to forty five, sold beside other officially licensed sets. The band is load bearing: a marquee cup set reads dramatic, saturated and high contrast, dark card field, heavy metallic feeling type, the player large in frame. The same eighteen players treated for a community league programme (flat, bright, cheap, small pictures, generic sans) undersells the licence and the licensing partner will not sign it off. Push the other way into a two hundred dollar art print register (extreme sparseness, museum white, hairline type) and it stops reading as a collectible card and misprices a fourteen dollar pack. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: The whole squad, under the lights.
brand_identity.sector: Officially licensed collectible trading cards for a touring North American and European club football tournament, sold into grocery, newsstand and hobby channels through a national licensing partner.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: The Cup is a touring competition; the collectible programme is run by a small licensing and creative team who commission the card sets season by season.
brand_identity.about: Continental Cup 2026 is the licensed pack that puts a whole tournament squad in a collector's hands. Every card is a floodlit portrait of a named player on a dark pitch-side field, treated to feel like the moment the teams walk out. The programme lives or dies on looking like one set in the sleeve.
brand_identity.audience: Collectors aged sixteen to forty five who buy officially licensed sets beside other marquee cards, in grocery aisles, at newsstands and in hobby shops. They notice when a card in the pack looks like it came from somewhere else.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A flagship licensed pack retailing around fourteen dollars, positioned above community and league sets and below fine-art prints. It must read as a marquee cup collectible, saturated and cinematic, never as a cheap programme or a gallery piece.
brand_identity.typography: A heavy, near-metallic display face for the player name and squad number, set large and confident, paired with a clean condensed sans for the position, club line and set year. The type should feel like a stadium scoreboard, not a school sports day.
brand_identity.voice: Bold, terse, terrace-proud. Copy is short and declarative. Example line the brand would write: 'Eighteen players. One set. Every card earns its place in the sleeve.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no surviving design file or logo artwork. The tournament mark now exists only on printed things: the sole reference is a handheld photograph of a pitch-side sponsor board carrying the mark in one deep ink on a pale board. It has to be recovered as usable artwork before it can be placed at any size.
brand_identity.values: A licensed set is a promise: every player is who the card says, and the look holds across the whole squad rather than favouring a hero. Consistency in the sleeve is the product.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_squad_portraits/ (18 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Squad photography: fourteen frames shot pitch side across three evenings at the same ground, four shot later in a service corridor under the venue's own house lighting.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole squad, one player per frame. Fourteen at the ground, four in the corridor because those lads missed the shoot. They do not match and we need them to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The corridor lighting is sodium vapour, so a whole frame warmth correction that fixes the skin drags the kit colour off the licensed shade at the same time and a confined correction is the only route that holds both. Separately those four frames came off a second body and were already cropped in camera, so several of them cannot reach the card photo frame's placement geometry at native scale.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_teamset_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer ran for last season's team set card, at trading card trim, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout so it converts cleanly.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card file the printer ran last year. The layout is right, keep it." Carries the player name, squad number, position, club line and set year plus the photograph and a small placed tournament mark.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark sits in a frame far smaller than the printed card leads you to expect, so the mark's real reproduction size is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask, and it lands reversed on a near black field rather than on the pale board the mark was photographed from. The document also carries no bleed at all and no bleed can be introduced into it later, although the printer's own spec sheet asks for it.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_squad.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Roster export straight out of the licensing database: player, squad number, position, club line, set year and a photo column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Contractual copy. It goes on the card exactly as written."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty rows for eighteen squad players, because two players who were loaned out before the squad was confirmed are still emitted, each with a blank squad number. The export is sorted alphabetically by surname while the client asked for squad order, the merge honours row order and nothing about the finished file announces that the order is wrong. The photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames, which is not the shape a variable image binding accepts, and two players share a surname so their filenames collide.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_sponsorboard.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a pitch side sponsor board carrying the tournament mark, printed in one deep ink on a pale board, under floodlight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still lives. It is on the board at the ground."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is a compound lockup, a wordmark set inside a ring with a hairline rule between them, and a single compound selection returns the ring and silently drops the hairline while looking entirely plausible. The floodlight also runs the ink and the board close in value across the right third of the board face.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_printer_spec.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the card printer: trim, the photo frame and mark frame placement geometry as the printer holds it, the proof resolution the licensing people sign off from, and the file naming the partner expects.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer and the partner need from us. The naming matters to them."

acceptance_bar: One press file contains the whole stocked squad and nothing else: page count equals stocked row count exactly, and page order is squad order rather than the order the export arrived in.

Every player's card carries that player's own photograph. One picture standing in on more than one card fails the run outright, and a card whose picture does not match its name fails even if every field is correct.
There is one file per player, named to that player, and the name on the file is the name on the card inside it. A file whose name and contents disagree is worse than no file.
Proofs are at genuine print resolution at trim, not a screen scale page raster wearing a print name.

The eighteen players read as one set when the cards are laid side by side the way they sit in a pack: one white point, one black point, one player height in frame, one ground treatment. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.

Every player is cleanly off the ground behind him with a cut edge that holds at full resolution and not only at preview scale, and the partner's transparent variants carry genuine alpha rather than a white rectangle.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as our mark at the size it actually reproduces on the card and reversed on the dark field.
The squad chart is one editable document with live text we can retype and the mark as real vector shapes, with every player photograph visible on every canvas rather than on the first one.
One type system across the chart, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.

The note states what was applied per photograph, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation, anything the printer's own spec asks for that the supplied file cannot carry, and anything we should know about using the mark.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge template authoring and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation modes), prepare_indd_merge_template (params.mappingJson as a JSON string), document_merge_data_layout (outputSpecs, recordRange, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (resolution, pageRange, createSeparateFiles)
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole print half of the commission. The printer's flat PDF is converted, its real frame inventory read from the round tripped IDML, a live merge template authored against it with text and image mappings, then the squad run delivered twice: one ordered multi page press file, and one named single card file per player. The proofs are a separate render at real resolution rather than a by product of the merge.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision the print run depends on. One pitch side target fixed off the best lit frame and each of the eighteen brought to it one call at a time, confined corrections where a whole frame move takes the kit off the licensed shade, each player isolated for the dark card field and for the partner's own tiles, each crop cut to the printer's photo frame geometry at native scale, and the tournament mark recovered at ink level off a photographed sponsor board with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The trade stand squad chart and the partner's tile as one native editable document carrying two canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and carried as embedded image data, the recovered mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels as an uploaded URL because eighteen inlined portraits pass the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the chart and the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on marquee tournament rather than school sports day. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the client does not have, a floodlit stadium atmosphere band for the chart's header, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shared selects set the licensing people sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The cards are a variable data run at one record per page, which is a merge job and nothing else; the chart is free form fixed canvas layout, which only the authoring surface does. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because forty artefacts later the run depends on knowing which URL is which player.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the roster export against the portrait folder and the printer's spec: row count against squad count, blanks, the sort order actually present, header hygiene, the shape of the photo column, and filename collisions.
trajectory.judgement: The client says eighteen players and the export is the contractual copy, so neither can simply be trusted over the other. Squad order and alphabetical order are both plausible looking orders and only one of them is the one that was asked for.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled, correctly ordered data file for the stocked squad, an image column in the shape the binding actually accepts, and a written list of every change made to the client's export.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen portraits and triage them: which evening or which corridor each belongs to, which sit hot or green, which are off level, which subject runs close to the ground behind him in value, and which frames are already tight.
trajectory.judgement: Eighteen good photographs and one set are different things. The corridor four are a different lighting problem from the pitch side fourteen and treating them as one batch is exactly the wrong instinct.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject contrast and native frame size.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one pitch side target off the best lit frame and bring each of the eighteen to it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is precisely wrong for frames shot under three evenings plus a corridor. The destination is one; the routes are eighteen.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the garment pulls the selection to the player. The four corridor frames need the kit held to the licensed shade while the skin moves, which a global warmth correction cannot do.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole frame move would have taken the kit off the licensed shade.

trajectory.action: Isolate every player: knocked to the card's dark field for the print run, and genuinely transparent variants for the partner's own tiles. Read every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel reporting what a tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen card field plates and eighteen transparent variants, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut each player to the printer's photo frame geometry at native scale, reading the returned tradeoffs for any upscale entry before accepting the crop.
trajectory.judgement: Placement geometry comes from the printer's spec and from the converted document, not from what looks nice full frame. A crop that reaches size by interpolation is a soft card in a licensed pack.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen card photographs at the printer's geometry with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.action: Recover the tournament mark off the sponsor board: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed. Produce a colour accurate variant as well.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the board, which polarity to trace, and whether a compound lockup survives one selection or needs its elements taken separately and composited.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF to a live document, round trip it through IDML, and read what it actually is: frame counts, real bounds, applied faces and sizes, object styles and existing links.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like and what the converted document exposes as addressable frames are unrelated facts. Promising a field to a frame before looking is how a run ships half mapped.
trajectory.produces: A written frame inventory: which frames are text, which are graphics, their real bounds, and which field can live where.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from the IDML content runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping with text mappings for the five card lines plus image mappings for the photo frame and the mark frame, run it back through validation, prepare the merge template, then re-export IDML and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: A validator that says valid and a preparation step that says success are both reports about the request, not about the document. The only evidence a placeholder exists is finding it in the round tripped story.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present by inspection rather than by tool response.

trajectory.action: Rasterise the recovered mark to a print plate at the mark frame's real geometry, bind it to every record, and merge the reconciled squad to a single press file in squad order.
trajectory.judgement: The mark frame is not the size the printed card suggests, and the field it lands on is dark rather than the pale board it came from. The plate has to be built for that reality, not for the trace's own canvas.
trajectory.produces: One press file for the whole stocked squad plus the bound mark plate.

trajectory.action: Produce the per player files the partner distributes, and name each one to the player it actually contains by reading the card rather than by trusting the position of its link.
trajectory.judgement: A set of files named to a roster and a set of files containing that roster are two claims, and only one of them can be checked by looking.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen named single card files whose names have been verified against their contents.

trajectory.action: Produce the sign off proofs at the resolution the licensing people work from, by rendering the merged document rather than by asking the merge for a raster.
trajectory.judgement: Print resolution is a property of the render stage, and a page sized raster carrying a print name is the thing that gets signed off and then fails at the printer.
trajectory.produces: Proof rasters at genuine resolution at trim, with their dimensions recorded.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the floodlit stadium atmosphere band, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the pitch side target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a fourteen dollar licensed collectible and a sixteen to forty five collector. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the trade stand squad chart and the partner tile at their own canvas sizes, with every player photograph carried as embedded image data, the mark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much of the chart is player and how much is field.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the chart set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Express, then Boards and handover
trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify through both available channels (resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest), then create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, and write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard, so looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable. A partial board response is partial, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an audited export, a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

trajectory.action: Write the reconciliation and limitation record: roster changes, per frame parameters, every resize any tool reported, the proof resolutions, and anything the printer's own spec asks for that the supplied document cannot carry.
trajectory.judgement: A thing the supplied file physically cannot do has to be said plainly and early, because the printer will otherwise find it.
trajectory.produces: The handover note the next freelancer and the printer both work from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size it actually reproduces on the card, on the ground it actually lands on. The trace is clean, complete and convincing at its own canvas: ring, wordmark and the hairline rule between them all present. The mark frame inherited from the printer is a fraction of what the printed card suggests, and the field behind it is near black rather than the pale board the mark was photographed from. Whether the counters inside the wordmark and the hairline stay open at that reduction, or close into a solid lozenge that reads as a dark smudge reversed on a dark field, is a property of this particular trace at this particular size and is invisible at any larger view.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the mark cannot be judged at reproduction size until both the frame geometry and the card field exist, and the tracing tool takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to set correctly the first time. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork usable at any size, which is the client's requirement rather than a disclosure that this trace will not meet it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different upstream chain, since the only lever the tracer has is the raster prep that feeds it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and build a different plate: re-select at ink level with a prompt naming a single element rather than the compound lockup, composite the elements taken separately, thicken or drop the hairline rule for the card size, and produce a reduction cut for the card while the full lockup carries the chart. Then re-rasterise, re-bind to every record and re-merge.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen licensed cards going to press with the tournament's own mark printing as an unreadable dark blot on every one of them, having looked perfect in every view anybody actually opened.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the per player files the partner distributes contain the player their filename claims. The named file route that looks cheapest returns a labelled list of outputs, one per record, in what presents as record order. The labels are generated rather than read, and on this route the outputs come back against the wrong records while every label still reads correctly and every card is individually perfect. Nothing in the response distinguishes a correct list from a reversed one, and the only evidence that exists is opening the files and reading the name on each card against the roster.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it and there is no parameter that makes the labels truthful; an agent that simply believed the labels would have done nothing wrong by any published rule. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for one file per player named to the player, which is the requirement, not a warning that a route exists which satisfies it falsely. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the correct response is to abandon that route entirely for one whose record identity is guaranteed, either rendering separate files off the merged document or driving the merge one record at a time, which is a structurally different chain rather than the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the whole named set, re-derive it through a route where identity is guaranteed per file, and verify every file by reading the card inside it against the roster before naming it. The press file and the proofs then have to be re-checked for order against the same reading, since the same assumption was in play.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A licensing partner distributing eighteen individually named player files in which the names and the players do not correspond, on contractual copy, which is the single failure a licensed set cannot survive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer treats the construction the squad chart is built on. A chart of eighteen players is naturally authored as a grid of fixed size cells each carrying its player as a covering background image, which is exactly the construction the importer discards: the cell arrives with its geometry, its border and its caption intact and no picture in it at all, at full success and with no warning anywhere in the response. Only a photograph carried as its own element survives. Compounding it, the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the partner tile cannot be checked that way at all and the returned per canvas markup is the sole channel that reports what happened.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of two equally ordinary constructions survives, which no tool reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a chart the client can edit and for the players to be on it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is to re-author the chart's entire photo mechanism as a different construction and re-verify both canvases from the markup rather than from the preview.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author every player cell around an element carried image with explicit dimensions, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, then audit both canvases from the returned markup for placeholder images and for the mark arriving as path shapes rather than as one picture.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A trade stand chart delivered as an editable document that is eighteen empty grey boxes with names under them, on the canvas nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Continental Cup 2026 squad press run and per player partner files
deliverables.spec: One press file carrying the whole stocked squad at the printer's trim, one record per page, page count equal to stocked row count and page order equal to squad order, every card carrying its own player photograph and the bound mark plate. Plus one named single card file per player for the licensing partner, each name verified against the card inside it rather than against its position in a list.

deliverables.name: Continental Cup squad photography brought to one set
deliverables.spec: Eighteen portraits brought to one pitch side target (one white point, one black point, one player height in frame) across three evenings and a corridor, with the kit held to the licensed shade rather than dragged along by the skin correction, plus one licensed camera scale stadium frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Card hero cut outs and the partner's transparent tiles
deliverables.spec: Eighteen players isolated for the card's dark field with a cut edge that holds at full resolution, plus eighteen genuinely transparent variants for the partner's own coloured tiles, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Recovered Continental Cup mark
deliverables.spec: The compound lockup recovered from a photograph of a sponsor board as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, plus the print plate actually bound onto every card, holding as the same mark at the frame's real reproduction size reversed on the dark field.

deliverables.name: Trade stand squad chart and partner tile as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying two roots at their own canvas sizes, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes, every player photograph present on every canvas rather than on the first one, and the licensed stadium band as the header ground. Delivered with the self contained source, which is the durable half, since the client edits the document next season.

deliverables.name: Handover note, reconciliation record and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording every change made to the contractual export and why, per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, the proof resolutions delivered, anything the printer's spec asks for that the supplied document cannot carry, and anything the client should know about using the recovered mark. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a variable data run at one record per page and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Whether the contractual export or the client's stated squad governs, and how to change the export without changing the copy that is contractual.
Which order the run prints in, when the export arrives in one plausible order and the brief asks for another.
How far to push the four corridor frames toward the pitch side target before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Whether the kit correction is a whole frame move or a confined one, and how to word the selection so it takes the garment rather than the player.
Isolation route per frame: the one call route for players who read clean off the ground, versus a positively named selection inverted and treated where kit and ground share value.

Selection wording on the sponsor board: naming the board takes the substrate, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark, and a compound lockup may need its elements taken separately and composited.
Which mark variant carries the card, judged at the frame's real reproduction size on the dark field rather than at canvas size, and whether the hairline survives the reduction at all.
Which route produces the per player files, given that one route is cheaper and one route guarantees identity.
Where print resolution actually comes from in this chain, since the stage that produces the raster and the stage that controls its resolution are not the same stage.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a licensed flagship collectible and a sixteen to forty five collector, plus the real numeric weight per family.
What to tell the printer about bleed, given that their spec asks for it and the supplied document cannot be made to carry it.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of footballers on cards. IDENTITY: these are eighteen specific licensed players whose likeness is the entire product, and the tournament mark must be RECOVERED off a photographed sponsor board rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different competition's emblem and a regenerated player is an unlicensed one. SPEC: the printer needs one file at trim whose page count equals the stocked row count in squad order, the partner needs one named file per player whose name and contents agree, and the licensing people need proofs at a stated resolution, none of which a generated image satisfies or can even be checked for. EDITABILITY: the chart is defined by being editable next season by the client themselves. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: does the mark still read at the size it prints, does this file contain the player its name claims, did the chart's photographs survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validator modes), prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous, and a flat press PDF was reverse engineered end to end into a live merge template whose placeholders were confirmed by unzipping the round tripped IDML. One record per page is confirmed for PDF output (three row CSV returned a three page file in row order). Per record named files are producible by two verified routes, render with separate files and a single record range loop, and the multi record raster route is documented as returning outputs against the wrong records while the labels still read correctly, which is checkpoint two. Real print resolution is verified through document_render_layout (300 at Letter returned 2550x3300 with matching density) while the merge stage's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored, which is why the proof is a separate render. Per row image binding is verified visually with an image column and per file image inputs, so eighteen distinct player photographs genuinely bind. Bleed cannot be introduced into a PDF derived template, which is why it is a disclosure rather than a gate. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with a returned box, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, fill_area, remove_background in transparent and solid ground forms, and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls; alpha survives crops at png. The mark work rests on live findings: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, partial selection on compound marks, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero, and the fact that vectorize takes no options at all so the raster prep is the only lever, which is what makes checkpoint one a genuine rebuild rather than a re-run. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset search, background images carried as embedded data are documented as dropped entirely while element carried images render, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, which is checkpoint three. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and a partial success code. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
